messages:
maria-g: Heads up — the canary deploy that flipped adaptive kernel routing is showing elevated KV cache evictions and a couple OOMs on long-context (16k tokens) runs this morning. Noticed latency spikes too.

zack: Repro'd locally on a 48GB A100 image with the canary binary. KV cache footprint jumps ~1.8x during kernel handoff windows.

maria-g: minimal logs — OOM from workspace allocator, then eviction storm. stack trace: `runtime::workspace::alloc_failed -> allocator::slab->evict -> kvcache::shard::drop`

profiler-bot: Profiling snapshot (short):
```
GPU memory used: 41.2GB / 48GB
Workspace peaks during decoding: +9.6GB
KV cache resident: 10.8GB -> after handoff: 19.5GB
Kernel switch time: 12.3ms (contended)
```

tony: That pattern smells like buffer duplication when we select a different kernel path (fp16->int8 fallback) — we may be allocating transient buffers without reuse. :thinking:

claire: Can we toggle the "reuse_transient_buffers" flag in runtime.yaml for the canary? If that suppresses duplication we'll know it's buffer reuse. Proposed quick config: 
```
runtime:
  kernel_routing:
    adaptive: true
    reuse_transient_buffers: true
  allocator:
    workspace_reserve_mb: 8192
    evict_threshold_pct: 0.85
```

maria-g: Pushed that toggle to canary (svc/canary-3). Watching. deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2070123456 -> svc/canary-3 started by maria-g.

dan-sre: Also saw more small allocations from the kernel when batch size changes mid-request (streaming tokens). Could be our batching heuristic spawning a temporary kernel with larger workgroup allocations. We should cap batch expansion during kernel handoff.

zack: Took a heap diff between baseline and canary: transient buffers labeled `kernel_tmp_buf` increased by ~6.5GB during handoff window. Patch idea: reuse kernel_tmp_buf from a workspace slab rather than fresh device malloc.

maria-g: Good call. Two-prong approach: 1) reuse_transient_buffers toggle immediate; 2) allocator change to increase workspace_reserve_mb to absorb handoff peak. But raising reserve trades memory away from prefix cache.

claire: Right — prefix/prompt cache hit-rate will fall if we increase reserve. Quick check: current prefix cache settings: shards=16, ttl=30m, max_per_shard=768MB. With +8GB reserve we lose ~500MB/shard effective. Hit-rate on 30m window is ~78% for our traffic; reducing per-shard by 35% would drop hit-rate to ~64% based on last simulation.

tony: Can we instead do a short TTL ramp-down for cold shards to free hot-shard pressure while keeping global capacity? e.g., dynamic-ttl: hot_shard_ttl=45m, cold_ttl=5m, shard_split_threshold=0.6. That keeps popular prefixes available but sacrifices long-tail.

zack: Simulation suggests dynamic TTL keeps effective hit-rate ~73% while freeing ~6GB memory. Worth trying before enlarging reserve.

maria-g: Canary update — enabled reuse_transient_buffers + dynamic TTL config. Observing for 30m.

profiler-bot: New snapshot (after toggles):
```
GPU memory used: 39.0GB / 48GB
Workspace peaks during decoding: +4.1GB
KV cache resident: 12.6GB
Kernel switch time: 8.1ms
```

dan-sre: Nice, OOMs have stopped in the canary logs and eviction rate halved. Latency back to baseline for most flows. :thumbsup:

claire: Ops note — this suggests long-term fix should be: 1) kernel path buffer reuse in allocator, 2) adjust batching heuristic to prefer in-place expansion (no new kernel instance) where possible, 3) keep dynamic TTL for prefix cache as an adaptive knob.

tony: I'll open a PR for allocator reuse + add tests to assert no new device allocs during kernel switch. Also will push a small change to batch growth policy: cap instantaneous growth to +30% of current batch unless steady-state tokens queued > X.

maria-g: Thanks. Follow-ups: zack plz run a few stress sims with 1) worst-case long-context tails, 2) mixed stream + batch workloads to validate. Put perf counters in canary for next 24h.

zack: On it. I'll post results in this thread.

maria-g: Closing note — avoid immediately bumping shard counts or permanent per-shard caps as first lever; prefer transient TTL-driven pressure relief and allocator reuse. We'll schedule a deeper postmortem if we see recurrence.

deploy-bot: Canary svc/canary-3 completed. All checks passed except transient increase in eviction rate (now resolved).
